responses.name: Tester 9

text.most: I used the commentary and study notes most along with the journal and bookmarks so that I could transcribe them into my bible journal
text.one: While I’ve loved reading through the commentaries and study notes and being able to sit with the passages, on busier days I’d love the option to have a more condensed version with main points and highlights so I can still stay on track.
text.confusing: Understanding how progress is tracked. I was looking for a way to be able to go back to my previous days of reading directly from the progress section but I couldn’t go back to it once I read it. However, I realized I could get back to it through Bible mode.
text.stuck: Using the highlighter. Tapping the verse to highlight was easy, although I wish I had the option to highlight a few words instead of the entire sentence. Also, when I tapped a verse and the screen with the highlighters came up, if I tapped the little arrow to pull the screen up, I was not able to pull it back down. I had to come out of the app to get back to the reading plan.
text.journalMore: Being able to copy and paste some of Scribes answers to the journal
text.rightMoment: The study notes icon placed next to the corresponding verses flowed so well and made for fluid reading
text.ordering: The only thing I’d suggest is explaining the reason the books are ordered and grouped the way they are so the reader has a clear understanding of why they’re ordered that way
text.anythingElse: Unfold is unlike any other Bible app I’ve used. I’m usually drawn to the aesthetics of something before I use it and often times I’d find something beautiful but it lacks depth. Unfold is set apart in that regard- its design reflects both the beauty AND the depth of scripture.

responses.musicPlayer: Pinned to the screen — always one tap away
